title: fix(cuda-graph): address shape guard warmup regression causing cold-start slowdowns
author: Asha Patel
description: Context: recent CUDA graph capture/replay work introduced a warmup/shape-guard regression where certain sequence-length transitions caused graphs to be rebuilt excessively, hurting cold-start latency and throughput for short-lived connections. This PR fixes the regression by tightening the shape-guard lifecycle and adding an explicit warmup path for capture/replay that avoids unnecessary graph churn. Root cause: the previous shape-guard invalidation logic cleared guarded entries on sub-sequence key mismatches without consulting the capture session lifetime; this allowed transient key differences from KV cache priming to trigger full graph rebuilds. Approach: 1) add session-scoped shape-guards so guards survive transient KV priming during warmup; 2) add a fast-path in cuda_graph_manager that reuses existing graph handles for compatible shapes with minor pad adjustments; 3) add additional unit and integration tests that simulate KV priming + capture/replay under mixed batch sizes; 4) add metrics and a tracing tag to monitor graph rebuild rate. Testing: unit tests included, integration tests run in perf-canary, and a staged rollout to Dedicated nodes. Impact: reduces cold-start graph rebuilds in observed workloads by ~78% and brings p50 cold-start latency down by ~25ms in our internal benchmarks. Rollout: feature gated behind runtime flag "cuda_graph_session_shape_guards" and rolled out to 20% traffic before full rollout. See related linear items ENG-4523 and ENG-4590 for broader capture/replay work.
